sentences.sentence: Marcel Siem held his nerve amid a late charge from Francesco Molinari to take the Open de France -- his first European Tour title for eight years.
The German finished on eight-under-par, one shot better than Molinari who recorded seven-under-par after producing a brilliant performance to deny Siem a second successive European Tour victory.
Siem, who previously won the Czech Open in 2004, had been leading since Friday but held off the late charge from Molinari to triumph on Sunday.
The Italian carded five birdies and a bogey to finish on seven-under-par.
"I just kept my composure," Siem said.
"I knew I had to hold my nerve and stay focused.
I managed to do that and I'm really happy with the way I played today."

Molinari, who was chasing a third consecutive victory after wins at the Italian Open and BMW PGA Championship, said: "I thought I was going to win until the last few holes, so it's a bit disappointing, but I'll take second place."
Another notable player at the tournament was Lee Westwood who came through an injury scare to continue his strong season.
Westwood, who won the WGC-HSBC Champions tournament earlier this month, was playing in his first tournament since injuring his ankle in the final round at the Dubai Desert Classic.
"It was a big relief to get through that round and it certainly wasn't the most comfortable day," Westwood said.
"But I'm glad it's behind me now and I can focus on this event and the rest of the season."
The highlight of the week had to be the performance by American rookie Ted Potter who became the PGA Tour's sixth first-time winner of 2012 with a four-under-par 68.
Potter, ranked 302nd in the world, outplayed more experienced players like Rory McIlroy and Lee Westwood to claim victory.

sentences.sentence: Among the 35,000 runners lining up at this Sunday's London Marathon, there'll be the usual pre-race nerves, waves of excitement, and focus on the task ahead.
This year, there will also be silence.

Six days after the tragic events in Boston, where two bombs exploded near the finish line of the Boston Marathon, killing three people and injuring hundreds more, London is hosting its annual marathon, and it is taking special measures to honor those affected by the attacks.

This year’s London Marathon is dedicated to the victims and first responders of the Boston Marathon bombings, and as part of their remembrance, organizers have asked all participants to observe a minute’s silence during the race, and run under the theme “Stronger Together.” Organizers of the marathon say that while the atmosphere at the start line might be subdued, once the race begins, the energy should be electric and positive.
The race, starting from Greenwich Park and finishing along The Mall, will see thousands of runners from around the world compete for a place on the street.
This year, however, has taken on an extra significance, with participants expected to run for peace and unity, and to pay tribute to those caught up in last week's tragedy.

At the start line, organizers will lead a moment’s silence before the race starts, and thousands of runners are expected to wear black solidarity ribbons to commemorate those killed and injured in Boston.
In addition, organizers say that heightened security measures are being implemented to ensure the safety of all participants, with increased searches and police presence throughout the course.

Despite the somber mood surrounding the event, organizers believe that the marathon can serve as an important step towards recovery, not only for the city of Boston but also for all of the United States.

The hearing was sponsored by advocates for consumer rights and was held in a crowded room on the third floor of the Rayburn House Office Building.
The purpose of the hearing was to address concerns over long tarmac delays.
A bill, sponsored by Senator Barbara Boxer (D-Calif.), proposes to allow fliers to deplane after three hours if the plane has been parked on the tarmac.
This bill would amend the Airline Safety and Federal Aviation Administration Extension Act of 2010, which currently allows airlines to hold passengers on the tarmac for up to four hours.
During the hearing, former American Airlines CEO Robert Crandall testified in favor of the three-hour limit, stating that it was necessary to protect passengers' rights.
He also expressed support for the bill, saying, "The current law is indefensible.
It needs to be changed.
Passengers should not be held on the tarmac for extended periods of time."
Another witness, John Geller, testified that routine delays are more pressing an issue than tarmac delays.
He stated, "While tarmac delays are a serious concern, they are only part of the larger problem of routine delays.
Airlines need to focus on reducing routine delays, which are more common and can last longer than tarmac delays."
Other witnesses included passengers who had experienced long tarmac delays and spoke about their experiences.
They described being stuck on the tarmac for several hours without food, water, or bathroom facilities.
They also mentioned that some airlines provide no information to passengers about why the delay is happening or when they will be able to disembark.
At the end of the hearing, Senator Boxer stated, "We are here today to discuss a serious issue that affects millions of Americans.

sentences.sentence: It’s set to be one of the most groundbreaking moments in humanity’s six decades of space exploration: Today SpaceX was due to land a rocket on a floating platform after launching.
But those looking forward to this pivotal moment will have to wait a little longer.
The rocket, a Falcon 9, was scheduled to launch from Cape Canaveral carrying a Dragon capsule, and then attempt to land on a drone ship located in the Atlantic Ocean.
However, the launch has been pushed back until Tuesday, January 6th at 11:18 AM GMT.
Originally planned for yesterday, January 3rd, the launch was postponed due to an engine issue.
SpaceX has faced similar delays in recent weeks, with two previous launches being postponed for the same reason.
The company aims to eventually have fully reusable rockets, and this test is an important step towards achieving that goal.

Following lift-off, the first stage of the Falcon 9 rocket will attempt to land on the autonomous spaceport drone ship, named Just Read the Instructions, which is stationed approximately 385 miles off the coast of Florida.
This will be the first time a rocket has attempted to land on a moving platform after launching into space.
CEO Elon Musk described the ambitious endeavor as having a “50/50” chance of success.
In a press conference, Mr Musk elaborated on the significance of the event:
“This is not just a big deal; it’s a巨无霸（jù wú bà）, a monster.
It’s really, really, really important,” he said.
The successful landing would be a significant breakthrough in space travel technology.
Currently, once a rocket leaves Earth’s atmosphere it cannot be reused.
This means that every time a mission requires a launch, a new rocket must be built.
This is not only expensive, but also environmentally unfriendly due to the use of vast amounts of fuel.

Natasha Smith recounted the experience on her blog and in an interview.

On Tuesday, November 7th, 2012, British student journalist Natasha Smith was attacked and nearly raped by a mob in Tahrir Square after what was supposed to be a joyous occasion—the announcement of Mohamed Morsi as the first democratically elected president of Egypt.
The incident sent shockwaves through the international community and raised serious questions about the safety of women in the Middle East.
According to Smith, the attack occurred after a large crowd in Tahrir Square began chanting "Down, down, down, down Mubarak!"
Smith, a freelance correspondent for the Guardian, was standing in the middle of the crowd when suddenly she heard someone scream, “Look, look, look!
A woman!” Smith turned around to see a group of men surrounding her, each trying to rip off her clothes.

In a blog post titled "Mob tried to strip me in Tahrir Square,” Smith recounts the harrowing experience: “There were several moments at which I thought she was going to die,” a friend told The Daily Telegraph.
"I couldn't believe it; these were Egyptian men who came to save me.” Egyptian bystanders stepped in to help and protect Smith from the mob.
Smith was able to escape with the help of the Egyptians who protected her and guided her away from the area.
She said, "I will always be grateful to those brave Egyptians who risked their lives to save mine."
The incident sparked outrage and condemnation throughout the international community.
Egyptian officials said they would do everything possible to find and punish the attackers.

sentences.sentence: The prosecutor in a rural California agricultural community says that police officers there preyed upon the poor, impounding their cars then selling the vehicles when the owners couldn't afford the fees.
Six officers, including the former police chief of King City and his successor, were arrested on Tuesday.

According to a CNN affiliate, the small department is already stretched thin after a number of recent high-profile arrests, including a local sheriff deputy accused of sexual misconduct and an officer facing charges related to domestic violence.
The scandal involving the King City police department has caused outrage among residents and has prompted a series of protests and rallies.
"The DA says officers would impound cars of people who couldn't pay release fees," stated Deputy District Attorney Scott Peterson.
"The impound lot owner would turn cars over to cops, who then sold or kept them."
The interim chief, identified as James Ertel, said he was not aware of any such practices taking place under his watch.
He told reporters that he had served as interim chief for just 45 days before stepping down, and during that time, he did nothing to support the impounding and selling of cars.
"Nothing I did or didn't do contributed to this situation," Ertel said in a statement.
"I did no wrong."

Among those arrested alongside Ertel and the former chief, Gary Walker, are two other officers who are currently still serving in the department, as well as two former officers who have since left the force.
All six individuals are being charged with grand theft and false imprisonment.
Peterson noted that the impounded vehicles were often left unattended for weeks, which allowed thieves to break into them and steal valuable items such as radios and GPS units.
The DA also stated that some of the impounded vehicles were so old that they could not be repaired or resold, and were therefore destroyed without any benefit to the department.
"This is a small department, and these kinds of incidents are straining our resources," Peterson added.

sentences.sentence: More than 450,000 Pakistanis have fled their homes for safer areas in the past two weeks as the military has attacked suspected anti-government militant hideouts in northwestern Pakistan, disaster management officials said Tuesday.
Many of the displaced civilians have moved to neighboring Kpk province, said Abdul Qader, an official from Pakistan's National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA).

In an operation codenamed Zarb-e-Azb, which translates roughly as “Strike of the Pulse,” the Pakistan military has stepped up its offensive against suspected insurgent hideouts in North Waziristan, a tribal area along the border with Afghanistan.
More than 250 insurgents have been killed, army says, and the Pakistani Taliban is among the targets.
Hundreds of civilians have also been killed or injured during the military operations that began last month, rights groups say.
"The scale of destruction is unprecedented," Muhammad Saleem, a doctor treating many of the injured, told Reuters news agency.
Pakistan’s military offensive is part of a wider push by the United States and NATO to root out al-Qaeda fighters and other militants who are hiding in the region.
In a televised address late Monday, Prime Minister Raja Pervez Ashraf urged people to stay calm and assured them that the government was taking necessary steps to ensure their safety.
"A significant number of displaced persons are in a vulnerable state due to harsh weather conditions and lack of essential facilities, such as food and shelter.
The government is providing them relief," he said.
The military operations are causing widespread disruption across a region already plagued by poverty and violence.
The area, which borders Afghanistan, has long been a haven for al-Qaeda and the Taliban, who use it as a base to launch attacks on neighboring countries, including Afghanistan and India.
The U.S. has been pressing Pakistan to step up its efforts against militant groups operating in the tribal areas.
